newsitem.title: USA: Minn. governor pegs budget surplus at $2.3 bln.
newsitem.headline: Minn. governor pegs budget surplus at $2.3 bln.

text.p: A new forecast for Minnesota indicates the state's budget surplus will grow to $2.3 billion by the end of the fiscal 1998-99 bienium, Gov. Arne Carlson announced Thursday.

The projection is nearly $900 million higher than the previous estimate of $1.4 billion. State finance commissioner Wayne Simoneau attributed the increase to a strong fourth quarter economy, low unemployment, an abundance of jobs, wage growth and a large number of year-end receipts.
The Republican governor proposed a $1.3 billion tax relief package that would be funded with the surplus.

"The hard working taxpayers who have stood with us as we have balanced the state budget deserve to receive a significant portion of the money back," Carlson said in a news release. "With a significant budget surplus, Minnesota's taxpayers should have some of their money returned.

The package called for a $750 million income tax rebate, $900 million in property tax relief for commercial, industrial and multi-family property over the next three years, a $150 million education tax credit, and $128 million in business and other tax reductions and higher education programs.
